question.problem: A surface $S$ is defined by $z=f(x,y).$ The curve $C$ is the intersection of $S$ with the plane $x=1.$ Given that the point $P(1,1,-1)$ lies on $C$, and that ${f}_{y}=\frac{{e}^{x}-{e}^{y}}{2x}+2y$, find the slope of the tangent to $C$ at $P.$
question.worked_solution:
The curve $C$ is the intersection of the surface $z=f(x,y)$ with the plane $x=1.$ Hence, the slope of the tangent to the curve $C$ at the point $P(1,1,-1)$ will be given by the partial derivative ${f}_{y}(1,1).$

To get the slope, we evaluate the partial derivative ${f}_{y}(x,y)$ at $(1,1):$

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}_{y}(1,1) & =\frac{{e}^{1}-{e}^{1}}{2(1)}+2(1) \\  & =0+2 \\  & =2\end{aligned}
$$
